Generate MILP code based on the provided description. Args: description: A description of the MILP to implement. Please generate the python or GAMS code to implement the provided model.

Generate a MILP model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under partial segment blockages on a high-speed railway line. 

Problem setting:
- A double-track high-speed railway line with stations indexed s ∈ S (ordered along the line). Trains run on a dedicated track per direction under normal conditions.
- A set of trains T, each with an origin, destination, direction (up/down), scheduled arrival/departure times at each station, and a scheduled route.
- A partial segment blockage occurs on a specific segment (between two consecutive block points/stations) on the up-direction track during a known time window [T_dis_start, T_dis_end]. During this window, trains scheduled on the up-direction cannot use their normal track on that segment, but may be rerouted to the opposite (down-direction) track within the disruption area.
- The dispatcher may: (i) retime arrivals/departures at stations, (ii) reorder trains at stations, (iii) reroute disrupted trains to the opposite track within the disrupted segment, (iv) cancel trains (optional).

Model components:
1. Train Rescheduling (TRP):
   - Variables: arrival time a_{t,s}, departure time d_{t,s}, running time r_{t,k} on segment k, dwell time w_{t,s}, rerouting binary u_{t,k} (1 if rerouted on segment k), cancellation binary x_t, train order binary o_{t,t',s} (1 if t precedes t' at station s).
   - Objective terms: weighted sum of delays (deviation from schedule), cancellations, and order changes.

2. Train Speed Management (TSMP):
   - Discretize time into small intervals n ∈ N of length Δ.
   - For each train t and each interval n: position p_{t,n}, speed v_{t,n}, acceleration a_{t,n} (use different symbol, e.g., acc_{t,n} or u_{t,n} for acceleration).
   - Kinematic constraints linearized: p_{t,n+1} = p_{t,n} + v_{t,n}*Δ + 0.5*acc_{t,n}*Δ², v_{t,n+1} = v_{t,n} + acc_{t,n}*Δ.
   - Bounds: 0 ≤ v_{t,n} ≤ v_max, acc_min ≤ acc_{t,n} ≤ acc_max.
   - Position must traverse from origin to destination and be consistent with arrival times at stations (must reach station s position P_s by arrival time a_{t,s}).

3. Coupling constraints:
   - Running time on segment k equals the time the speed profile takes to traverse from the start to end position of segment k.
   - If rerouted, the train's position passes through the segment during the disruption time window on the opposite track.
   - Dwell time at station s: d_{t,s} - a_{t,s} ≥ min_dwell, and equals dwell time variable w_{t,s}.

4. Conflict resolution:
   - Forbid two trains (any direction) from occupying the same position at the same time (or maintain minimum headway).
   - On the disrupted segment during the disruption window: trains going up (rerouted) and trains going down (normal) share the single available track. Use binary occupancy variables and enforce at most one train in the segment per time.
   - At stations, headway constraints between consecutive departures/arrivals based on train order.

5. Disruption window:
   - If a train would be on the disrupted segment at time n (i.e., p_{t,n} is within segment k and n is in [T_dis_start/Δ, T_dis_end/Δ]), then either the train is rerouted (u_{t,k}=1) or its schedule avoids the time (which may be infeasible, enforced by constraints).

Objective: minimize α * Σ (delay of train t) + β * Σ (energy consumption approximated by Σ acc_{t,n}² or using tractable linear proxy Σ v_{t,n}) + γ * Σ (cancellation penalties) + δ * Σ (order change penalties).

Make reasonable assumptions where information is missing and clearly state them. Assume a single line with one disrupted segment, finite planning horizon, discrete time steps.
